transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to discuss the disposition of Batch B-417. As we all know, the batch contains 1,200 molded housings currently on quality hold due to a packaging-label printer outage. The dimensional inspection results are within our internal specification, so the product itself is conforming. However, before I can approve the final batch disposition and close the batch record, we need to complete the routine disposition review, which includes checking with packaging engineering and the customer quality liaison. Can someone from packaging engineering give us an update on the label printer situation and whether the labeling issue has been resolved?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important. My packaging shift log shows that exactly 240 housings were packed while the printer was malfunctioning, and their labels lack the required machine-readable lot code. Procedure requires those 240 units to be relabeled after a 2-hour line-clearance and printer-setup job, followed by barcode verification. I completed the log this shift, but it has not yet been uploaded to the batch record, so that information isn't visible there yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something important that I haven't yet attached to the batch record. This morning I received a signed customer amendment stating that the 240 relabeled housings may be released only after exactly 20 of them pass customer reapproval inspection. The amendment permits the other 960 correctly labeled housings to be released separately. I will make sure the amendment is attached to the batch record as part of this disposition review.
transcript.speaker: A3
